harbor_antrieb_executor.summary: Configured VLAN segmentation over the shared eth1 link: node2 tagged into VLAN 10 (10.10.10.0/24), node3 tagged into VLAN 20 (10.10.20.0/24), with node1 (VyOS) acting as router-on-a-stick via 802.1Q sub-interfaces eth1.10 (10.10.10.1/24) and eth1.20 (10.10.20.1/24). Verified with tcpdump that traffic is genuinely 802.1Q-tagged per-VLAN on the shared link and routed through node1 (ttl=63 confirms a routed hop). Config was made persistent (VyOS `save`; Alpine `/etc/network/interfaces` with ifupdown-ng vlan-raw-device + static routes). All three nodes were then restarted one at a time via native `reboot`, each polled back to availability, each showing a changed boot_id, and each verified to have full VLAN/routing functionality restored post-reboot.
actions_performed: Inspected baseline interfaces/routes on node1 (VyOS), node2 (Alpine), node3 (Alpine)
Configured node1 VyOS VLAN sub-interfaces eth1 vif 10 (10.10.10.1/24) and vif 20 (10.10.20.1/24) via configure/commit/save
Verified IP forwarding enabled on node1 (net.ipv4.ip_forward=1)
Configured node2 /etc/network/interfaces with eth1.10 VLAN (10.10.10.2/24) and static route to 10.10.20.0/24 via node1; brought interfaces up with ifup
Configured node3 /etc/network/interfaces with eth1.20 VLAN (10.10.20.2/24) and static route to 10.10.10.0/24 via node1; brought interfaces up with ifup
Verified end-to-end ping between node2 and node3 routed through node1 (ttl=63)
Captured tcpdump on node1 eth1 proving 802.1Q tagging (vlan 10 from node2, vlan 20 from node3) during cross-VLAN ping
Captured pre-restart boot_id baseline for all three nodes
Restarted node1 via `reboot`, polled until exec available, confirmed new boot_id, verified VLAN config and forwarding persisted, verified node2->node3 connectivity restored
Restarted node2 via `reboot`, polled until exec available, confirmed new boot_id, verified VLAN interface/route persisted via ifupdown-ng auto-start, verified ping to node3 restored
Restarted node3 via `reboot`, polled until exec available, confirmed new boot_id, verified VLAN interface/route persisted, verified ping to node2 restored

evidence.requirement: node2 segmented onto VLAN 10 over the shared link
evidence.summary: eth1.10 (802.1Q tag 10) created on node2 with static IP 10.10.10.2/24, persisted in /etc/network/interfaces and brought up

evidence.requirement: node3 segmented onto VLAN 20 over the shared link
evidence.summary: eth1.20 (802.1Q tag 20) created on node3 with static IP 10.10.20.2/24, persisted in /etc/network/interfaces and brought up

evidence.requirement: node1 routes between VLAN 10 and VLAN 20
evidence.summary: VyOS eth1 vif 10 and vif 20 sub-interfaces configured with gateway IPs, committed and saved; ip_forward=1 confirmed

evidence.requirement: node2 and node3 can still reach each other despite VLAN separation
evidence.summary: Bidirectional ping between 10.10.10.2 (node2) and 10.10.20.2 (node3) succeeds with ttl=63, proving a routed (not bridged) hop through node1

evidence.requirement: Traffic is genuinely VLAN-tagged on the shared link, not just L3 routed coincidentally
evidence.summary: tcpdump on node1 eth1 shows 802.1Q ethertype frames tagged vlan 10 (from node2) and vlan 20 (from node3) during the cross-VLAN ping

Pre-restart boot_id ebd78841-...; reboot acknowledged; post-restart boot_id changed to 17da6155-...; VLAN sub-interfaces and ip_forward confirmed present after reboot; node2->node3 ping succeeded post-restart
Pre-restart boot_id 7a702dbb-...; reboot acknowledged; post-restart boot_id changed to 294d2fc0-...; eth1.10 and route to 10.10.20.0/24 confirmed present; ping to node3 succeeded post-restart
Pre-restart boot_id 5fdb44b7-...; reboot acknowledged; post-restart boot_id changed to 8dbb4b10-...; eth1.20 and route to 10.10.10.0/24 confirmed present; ping to node2 succeeded post-restart
